new_statements.relation_note: The catalog record for Maria has an empty rule; Dutton 1970 supplies the first explicit statement: not tonal, stress phonemic (lexical), with a like-vowel-sequence sub-rule and stress-marked wordlist data. Nothing to contradict.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Maria (with Doromu, Kwale and Humene) is not tonal; word stress is phonemic (contrastive), so no placement rule is given. The only positional statement is that in a sequence of two like vowels the stress falls on the second vowel (unless a glottal stop separates them). The survey wordlists (Appendix 3.9, pp. 951-975) mark primary stress on Maria forms from four dialect villages (Maranomu No. 1 = Didigaru, Maria, Maiagolo = Imila, Uderi), and the mark falls on different syllables in different words and dialects (e.g. p. 951 'ame 'man', 'oue 'woman', 'maru?a 'husband', ba'ba?e / 'baba?e 'father', 'ama vs a'ma?e 'mother', u'boma 'child'), consistent with lexically placed stress.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not discussed; only primary stress is marked.
new_statements.exceptions: Sketch is explicitly provisional: 'based on survey materials and need to be checked against more extensive material'; stress is said to 'seem' phonemic. Vowels [ə] and [ɒ] appear only in unstressed syllables (Didigaru dialect).
new_statements.identity_note: Dutton 1970's phoneme sketch (p. 917) is of the Didigaru dialect of Maria (Maranomu No. 1), with notes on the Imila and Uderi dialects; the stress statement on p. 916 is made jointly for the Kwalean (Kwale, Humene) and Manubaran (Doromu, Maria) languages of Rigo; the wordlists (pp. 951-975) cover four Maria villages: Maranomu No. 1, Maria, Maiagolo, Uderi. Dutton 1975 (p. 636) lists seven Maria dialects (Didigaru, Maria, Gebi, Oibu, Amota, Imila, Uderi).

audit.reasoning: (1) Quote verified verbatim on p. 916 of the Dutton 1970 PDF we hold (page scan and text), Maria section on p. 917 as located. (2) The classification 'lexical' rests on a 1970 survey-based phoneme sketch whose author hedges the claim ('seems to be phonemic', 'need to be checked'); but per Glottolog 5.3 and Dutton 1975:636 (downloaded now from sealang, no later description of Maria exists, so it is very probably the best available source and is. (3) Nothing found contradicts the classification; the only stated regularity (like-vowel sequences stressed on the second vowel) is already in the record's the primary-stress rule. list of works to obtain is limited to sister-language Doromu-Koki grammars (family-level check) and an unverifiable SIL-PNG listing check; none is a Maria stress description. Hence 'thin' (old, hedged survey sketch, nothing better exists) with no ac
